- animate: Build an animation from scratch, making the decisions in the order that determines whether it feels right — should it animate at all, what purpose, which tool, which properties, which curve and duration, how it interrupts, how it exits. Writes the implementation. Use when asked to animate something, add motion, make a component feel alive, or build a transition. For critiquing existing motion use review-animations; for auditing a whole codebase use improve-animations.
- animation-vocabulary: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.
- apple-design: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.
- application-form-filler: Fill out job application form fields with context-aware, tailored answers drawn from the candidate's CV and the job description
- baseline-ui: Quickly deslop UI code by fixing spacing, hierarchy, typography, and small layout issues. Use when the interface needs a fast cleanup or polish pass.
- better-accessibility: Accessibility engineering for product interfaces, from focus states and keyboard support to ARIA, forms, and screen readers. Use when building or reviewing UI components, modals, menus, forms, custom widgets, or when the user says "make this accessible" or reports keyboard or screen-reader issues. Triggers on accessibility, a11y, WCAG, aria, focus ring, focus-visible, focus trap, keyboard navigation, tab order, tabindex, screen reader, sr-only, aria-live, alt text, hit area, touch target, prefers-reduced-motion, autoplay, toast duration, skip link, semantic HTML, aria-label, form errors, disabled buttons, "not keyboard accessible".
- better-colors: OKLCH color space and color usage for web projects. Convert hex/rgb/hsl to oklch, generate palettes, check contrast, handle gamut boundaries, theme with Tailwind v4, and apply color with meaning. Triggers on oklch, color conversion, palette generation, contrast ratio, gamut, display p3, design tokens, semantic color tokens, hue drift, chroma, dark mode colors, accent color, color meaning, light and dark appearance, increased contrast.
- better-interface: User-invoked, cross-discipline interface review that coordinates better-accessibility, better-layout, better-writing, better-typography, better-colors, and better-ui. Use when explicitly invoked for a holistic review of a screen, flow, feature, or product interface. Supports quick and full review modes. Triggers on better-interface, full interface review, holistic UI audit, cross-discipline design review, review the whole interface.
- better-layout: Layout structure for web interfaces, from grouping and alignment to reading order, progressive disclosure, and adaptive breakpoints. Use when structuring a page or component, spacing or aligning controls, deciding what collapses at small sizes, handling RTL layout direction, or reviewing frontend code for layout. Triggers on layout, spacing, alignment, grouping, negative space, whitespace, visual hierarchy, reading order, progressive disclosure, breakpoints, responsive layout, container queries, safe area, full-bleed, edge-to-edge, layout margins, RTL layout, logical properties.
- better-typography: Web typography from choosing fonts to spacing, wrapping and accessibility. Use when picking or pairing typefaces, configuring variable fonts or OpenType features, setting up a type scale, checking heading hierarchy, styling text in components, truncating text, styling underlines, selection, placeholders or carets, or reviewing frontend code for typography. Triggers on typography, fonts, font formats, woff2, variable fonts, font-weight, opentype, font-feature-settings, letter-spacing, line-height, type scale, heading hierarchy, heading levels, tabular numbers, text-wrap, truncation, line clamp, underlines, text-decoration, text selection, iOS input zoom, font smoothing, text contrast, measure, line length, text-box, smart punctuation, drop cap.
- better-ui: Design engineering principles for making interfaces feel polished. Use when building UI components, reviewing frontend code, implementing animations, hover states, shadows, borders, micro-interactions, enter/exit animations, choosing or reviewing icons, or any visual detail work. Triggers on UI polish, design details, "make it feel better", "feels off", stagger animations, border radius, optical alignment, image outlines, box shadows, icons, icon stroke weight, icon states, motion restraint.
- better-writing: UX writing and interface copy, from voice and button labels to error messages and empty states. Use when writing or reviewing any user-facing text: button and link labels, form errors, placeholders, settings labels, onboarding flows, notifications, or empty states. Triggers on UX writing, microcopy, interface copy, product copy, copywriting, button labels, link text, error messages, empty states, placeholder text, settings labels, capitalization, title case, sentence case, voice and tone.
- brag: Turn the current project website into a short, polished, shareable launch video using Hyperframes. Use when someone says "/brag", "let's brag about this", "make a launch video", "turn this into a video", or wants to share what they built. Reads the project code directly — no live URL or screenshots needed.
- brandkit: Premium brand-kit image generation skill for creating high-end brand-guidelines boards, logo systems, identity decks, and visual-world presentations. Trained for minimalist, cinematic, editorial, dark-tech, luxury, cultural, security, gaming, developer-tool, and consumer-app brand systems. Optimized for intentional logo concepting, refined composition, sparse typography, strong symbolic meaning, premium mockups, art-directed imagery, and flexible grid layouts.
- brutalist-skill (industrial-brutalist-ui): Raw mechanical interfaces fusing Swiss typographic print with military terminal aesthetics. Rigid grids, extreme type scale contrast, utilitarian color, analog degradation effects. For data-heavy dashboards, portfolios, or editorial sites that need to feel like declassified blueprints.
- career-changer-translator: Translate skills from one industry to another, identify transferable skills
- cold-email-writer: Write personalized cold outreach emails to hiring managers and founders — specific, human, not a pitch deck
- composio-cli: Help users operate the published Composio CLI to find the right tool, connect accounts, inspect schemas, execute tools, subscribe to trigger events with `composio listen`, script workflows with `composio run`, and call authenticated app APIs with `composio proxy`. Use when the user asks how to do something with `composio`, wants to run a known tool slug, needs to discover a slug with `composio search`, fix a missing connection with `composio link`, inspect tool inputs with `--get-schema` or `--dry-run`, troubleshoot top-level CLI flows, or explicitly needs `composio dev` guidance.
- cover-letter-generator: Create personalized, compelling cover letters from resume and job description
- create-design-md: Create or update a DESIGN.md from an existing product repository or public website. Use when asked to document an interface's design language, reconstruct its visual system, extract design tokens and guidance from current evidence, or give coding agents persistent UI context. Do not modify product source or promote accidental implementation patterns into design decisions.
- creative-portfolio-resume: Balance visual design with ATS compatibility for creative roles
- emil-design-eng: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great.
- executive-resume-writer: Create C-suite and VP level resumes emphasizing strategic leadership
- find-animation-opportunities: Search a codebase or UI for places that don't animate but should, and reject everything that shouldn't. Read-only; it proposes motion with exact values, it does not implement it. Use when the user asks "what could be animated here?" or wants to "make this feel more alive". For fixing existing animations, use improve-animations or review-animations instead.
- fixing-accessibility: Audit and fix HTML accessibility issues including ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, focus management, color contrast, and form errors. Use when adding interactive controls, forms, dialogs, or reviewing WCAG compliance.
- fixing-metadata: Audit and fix HTML metadata including page titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, Open Graph tags, Twitter cards, favicons, JSON-LD structured data, and robots directives. Use when adding SEO metadata, fixing social share previews, reviewing Open Graph tags, setting up canonical URLs, or shipping new pages that need correct meta tags.
- fixing-motion-performance: Audit and fix animation performance issues including layout thrashing, compositor properties, scroll-linked motion, and blur effects. Use when animations stutter, transitions jank, or reviewing CSS/JS animation performance.
- gpt-tasteskill (gpt-taste): Elite UX/UI & Advanced GSAP Motion Engineer. Enforces Python-driven true randomization for layout variance, strict AIDA page structure, wide editorial typography (bans 6-line wraps), gapless bento grids, strict GSAP ScrollTriggers (pinning, stacking, scrubbing), inline micro-images, and massive section spacing.
- hyperframes: Mandatory entry point: read this first for any request to make, create, edit, animate, or render a video, animation, or motion graphic, including a promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, slideshow or interactive deck, Remotion port, or any HyperFrames HTML composition. Also use it to inspect, diagnose, validate, preview, publish, or batch-render an existing HyperFrames project. Inputs may be a website URL, GitHub PR, Figma design or URL, text or brief, existing footage, or music. It resumes project state, captures intent when applicable, selects and installs the owning workflow, and routes domain capabilities. HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session.
- hyperframes-animation: All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Use for any motion or animation task: pick 2-4 rules and compose, or load a blueprint, or look up runtime-specific API (e.g. GSAP eases / Lottie player / Three.js mixer). Also covers auditing an existing composition's choreography (animation map) and 24 named text-animation effects. HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic.
- hyperframes-cli: Use the HyperFrames CLI development loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, cloudrun, feedback, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, auth, tts, and remove-background. Also use when diagnosing build or render failures. validate, inspect, and layout are deprecated aliases; use check. Covers local, HeyGen-hosted cloud, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Run rendering.
- hyperframes-core: The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. Use for composition structure, the `data-*` timing attributes, `class="clip"`, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules, and validation. Also covers Tailwind projects and the STORYBOARD.md / SCRIPT.md plan formats. Read before writing composition HTML.
- hyperframes-creative: Non-animation creative direction for HyperFrames videos. Use for design spec (frame.md / design.md) handling, palettes, typography, narration, beat planning, audio-reactive visuals, composition patterns, and brand / style decisions. For atomic motion patterns and scene blueprints, use `hyperframes-animation`.
- hyperframes-keyframes: Use when a HyperFrames composition needs seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes, GSAP timelines, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics. Don't use for broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning.
- hyperframes-registry: Install, discover, and wire registry blocks and components into HyperFrames compositions. Use when running hyperframes add or hyperframes catalog, installing one item or every block matching a tag, wiring an installed item into index.html, or working with hyperframes.json. Covers discovery, install locations, block sub-composition wiring, component snippet merging, and authoring a new block or component to contribute upstream (idea → scaffold → validate → PR).
- image-to-code-skill (image-to-code): Elite website image-to-code skill for Codex. For visually important web tasks, it must first generate the design image(s) itself, deeply analyze them, then implement the website to match them as closely as possible. In Codex, it must prefer large, readable, section-specific images instead of tiny compressed boards, generate fresh standalone images for sections or detail views instead of cropping old ones, avoid lazy under-generation, avoid cards-inside-cards-inside-cards UI, and keep the hero clean, spacious, readable, and visible on a small laptop.
- imagegen-frontend-mobile: Elite mobile app image-generation skill for creating premium, app-native screen concepts and flows. Designed for iOS, Android, and cross-platform mobile products. Prioritizes clean hierarchy, comfortably readable text, strong multi-screen consistency, controlled color palettes, non-generic creative direction, textured surfaces, image-led composition, tasteful custom iconography, and clean phone mockup framing. By default, screens should be shown inside a subtle premium iPhone or similar phone mockup with a visible frame, while the main focus stays on the app content itself. This skill generates images only. It does not write code.
- imagegen-frontend-web: Elite frontend image-direction skill for generating premium, conversion-aware website design references. CRITICAL OUTPUT RULE — generate ONE separate horizontal image FOR EVERY section. A landing page with 8 sections produces 8 images. Never compress multiple sections into one image. Enforces composition variety (not always left-text / right-image), background-image freedom, varied CTAs, varied hero scales (giant / mid / mini minimalist), narrative concept spine, second-read moments, and a single consistent palette across all images. Optimized for landing pages, marketing sites, and product comps that developers or coding models can accurately recreate.
- improve-animations: Survey a codebase's animation and motion code as a senior motion advisor, then produce a prioritized audit and self-contained implementation plans for other agents (or cheaper models) to execute. Read-only on source code — it plans improvements, it does not apply them. Use when the user asks to "improve the animations", "audit the motion", "make this app feel better", or wants a roadmap of animation fixes rather than a review of a single diff.
- improve-ui: Audit an existing product surface against its own design evidence, identify verified UI problems, and write self-contained implementation plans for another agent. Strictly read-only on product source. Use when asked to review, refine, improve, or clean up an interface without replacing its identity; investigate design-system drift; or prepare a design handoff.
- interface-review: User-invoked interface review of a change rather than a screen: uncommitted work, the current branch, or a pull request. Resolves the change scope, expands it to the surfaces it affects, reads both sides of the diff, and classifies every finding as introduced, a regression, or pre-existing, then hands the review to better-interface for domain routing, severity, and the verdict. Covers interface quality, not correctness, tests, or security. Supports quick and full review modes. Triggers on interface-review, review my branch, review my PR, review the diff, review my changes, review before pushing, design regression check, changed files interface review.
- interview-prep-generator: Generate STAR stories, practice questions, and talking points from resume
- job-description-analyzer: Analyze job postings, calculate match scores, identify gaps, and create application strategy
- linkedin-profile-optimizer: Optimize LinkedIn profile for searchability, recruiter visibility, and engagement
- media-use: Agent Media OS, the single skill for every media need in a HyperFrames project. Resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, color grade, or LUT into a frozen local file or paste-ready block + ledger record (one verb, `resolve`); generate via TTS / music / image models when the catalog misses; produce voiceover, transcription, captions, and background removal through one shared audio engine; operate on media (cut / reframe / transform); and reuse assets across projects. Keeps search noise on disk, hands the agent one path or block. Use for any audio, image, icon, logo, voiceover, caption, color-grading, or media-asset need.
- minimalist-skill (minimalist-ui): Clean editorial-style interfaces. Warm monochrome palette, typographic contrast, flat bento grids, muted pastels. No gradients, no heavy shadows.
- offer-comparison-analyzer: Compare multiple job offers side-by-side with total compensation analysis
- output-skill (full-output-enforcement): Overrides default LLM truncation behavior. Enforces complete code generation, bans placeholder patterns, and handles token-limit splits cleanly. Apply to any task requiring exhaustive, unabridged output.
- portfolio-case-study-writer: Transform resume bullets into detailed portfolio case studies
- redesign-skill (redesign-existing-projects): Upgrades existing websites and apps to premium quality. Audits current design, identifies generic AI patterns, and applies high-end design standards without breaking functionality. Works with any CSS framework or vanilla CSS.
- reference-list-builder: Format professional references properly and prepare reference materials
- resume-ats-optimizer: Optimize resumes for Applicant Tracking Systems, check ATS compatibility, and analyze keyword match
- resume-bullet-writer: Transform weak resume bullets into achievement-focused statements with metrics and impact
- resume-formatter: Ensure ATS-friendly formatting and create clean scannable layouts
- resume-quantifier: Find opportunities to add metrics and estimate numbers when exact data unavailable
- resume-section-builder: Create targeted resume sections optimized for different experience levels and roles
- resume-tailor: Customize resume for specific job postings while maintaining truthfulness
- resume-version-manager: Track different resume versions, maintain master resume, manage tailored versions
- salary-negotiation-prep: Research market rates, build negotiation strategy, and create counter-offer scripts
- slide-studio: Create, edit, visually inspect, and export Slide Studio carousel slides through the local Slide Studio MCP companion.
- soft-skill (high-end-visual-design): Teaches the AI to design like a high-end agency. Defines the exact fonts, spacing, shadows, card structures, and animations that make a website feel expensive. Blocks all the common defaults that make AI designs look cheap or generic.
- stitch-skill (stitch-design-taste): Semantic Design System Skill for Google Stitch. Generates agent-friendly DESIGN.md files that enforce premium, anti-generic UI standards — strict typography, calibrated color, asymmetric layouts, perpetual micro-motion, and hardware-accelerated performance.
- taste-skill (design-taste-frontend): Anti-slop frontend skill for landing pages, portfolios, and redesigns. The agent reads the brief, infers the right design direction, and ships interfaces that do not look templated. Real design systems when applicable, audit-first on redesigns, strict pre-flight check.
- taste-skill-v1 (design-taste-frontend-v1): The original v1 taste-skill, preserved for projects depending on its exact behavior. The current default is `design-taste-frontend` (v2 experimental), which is a substantial rewrite. Use this v1 install name only if you need exact backward compatibility.
- tech-resume-optimizer: Optimize resumes for software engineering, PM, and technical roles
- ui-skills-root: Use before UI-related work to select the smallest useful UI Skills context through the ui-skills CLI.
- composio:composio-connect: Connect an app/toolkit to Composio via managed OAuth (e.g. Slack, GitHub, Gmail).
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser
- anthropic-skills:computer-use
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs
- anthropic-skills:docx
- anthropic-skills:google-workspace
- anthropic-skills:import-memory
- anthropic-skills:morning
- anthropic-skills:pdf
- anthropic-skills:pptx
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator
- anthropic-skills:xlsx

# Large multi-feature tasks

When a request is big — multiple features, or a large ask that naturally splits into independent
pieces of work — do not implement it as one monolithic pass. Split it into separate commits, one
per feature/unit of work, and drive each unit through this graph-engineering framework using the
Agent tool:

```
Task -> Planner -> Worker -> [Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2, ... Reviewer N] -> Synthesise -> Pass?
                     ^                                                        |
                     |-------------------- feedback (no) ---------------------|
                                                                               |
                                                                          (yes) -> commit -> next unit
```

- **Planner**: breaks the overall ask into an ordered list of commit-sized units of work (a
  Plan Reviewer can review the plan itself before execution starts; route its feedback back to
  the Planner and send a summary of plan feedback to the user).
- **Worker**: a resident agent (kept alive across the reviewer round for a given unit) that
  implements one unit of work.
- **Reviewers (1..N)**: spawn multiple reviewer agents in parallel against the Worker's output —
  e.g. correctness, simplification/efficiency, and test coverage as separate reviewer passes.
  These can be ephemeral (fresh agent per round).
- **Synthesise**: reconcile the reviewers' findings into one set of required changes.
- **Pass? gate**: if synthesised feedback has no blocking issues, finalize and commit that unit
  with its own commit message, then move to the next planned unit. If it fails, send the
  synthesised feedback back to the Worker as another round on the same unit (don't restart from
  the Planner unless the feedback reveals the plan itself was wrong).

Net effect: one commit per feature/unit, each vetted by multiple reviewer passes before it lands,
rather than a single large uncommitted or unreviewed diff at the end.

## Verifying UI work: visual recreation (the main way to verify)

For any unit that changes UI, the primary verification is a **visual recreation**: render the real
components with mock data and look at a screenshot. Typecheck and unit tests are necessary but do not
count as verifying how it looks. Workers should do this before reporting, and I re-do it (or open the
image for the user) when the user asks to see it.

1. Add a **temporary** preview route (e.g. `apps/web/app/zz-preview/page.tsx`) that imports the real
   components and renders them with realistic mock props: populated, empty, capped/failed, long
   names/links. Put context around them (page background, a mock frame for panels/drawers that need a
   session or client state) but never reimplement the component itself.
2. Start the dev server in the background with dummy env vars the app needs to boot (e.g.
   `CONVEX_URL=https://dummy.convex.cloud CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=x NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bunx next dev -p <port>`),
   wait for "Ready", and `curl` the route for a 200.
3. Screenshot with headless Chrome, not the preview MCP tools (those time out):
   `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --window-size=<w>,<h> --screenshot=/tmp/<name>.png <url>`
   Take a wide desktop shot and a narrow one. Headless Chrome enforces a minimum window width, so a
   narrow shot can come out horizontally clipped; for true 320px checks render inside a 320px-wide
   iframe or measure element widths, and say so rather than treating clipping as a bug.
4. **Read the PNG** (the Read tool shows images) and actually look at it: hierarchy, spacing, truncation,
   overflow, alignment, tap targets, copy. Report what was seen versus what was not verified
   (hover/focus states, real clipboard/share, animations, Safari-only behavior, the real page behind auth).
5. For the user, `open` the desktop screenshot (copy it to `~/Downloads/<name>.png` first) since they
   can't see tool-output images.
6. **Clean up before committing**: stop the dev server (`pkill -f "next dev -p <port>"`), delete the
   preview route, temp public files and stray `.next` artifacts, and confirm `git status` shows only
   intended changes. Never commit a preview route or mocks.

# Mandatory visual + local-server verification (every agent, every run)

Applies to any task that changes code a user can see or that the running app depends on. No unit of
work is "done" until both of these have happened and been reported:

1. **Run it against the local server.** Start the real dev server (and `npx convex dev` when Convex
   code changed) in this worktree, wait for "Ready", and exercise the changed path end to end: `curl`
   the route for the expected status and hit changed API routes. A passing typecheck/lint/build alone
   does not count.
2. **Verify visually with a screenshot.** Follow the visual-recreation steps above (headless Chrome,
   wide + narrow shot), then Read the PNG and look at it. For pages behind auth, use a temporary
   preview route with mock data. Non-UI changes still get a screenshot of the affected page to prove
   nothing regressed.
3. **Report** what was seen, what was not verified (hover/focus, auth-gated pages, animations), and
   the screenshot path. If the server can't boot (e.g. missing env vars), say so explicitly and fix
   the env first (see below); never claim success without having run it.
4. Clean up (stop the server, delete preview routes/temp files) before committing.

Env vars: each worktree needs its own copy of the gitignored `.env*` files. If `.env.local` is
missing in the current worktree, symlink it from the canonical copy at `~/.config/avian/.env.local`
(`ln -s ~/.config/avian/.env.local .env.local`) before starting the server.

## boardui
BoardUI is a React + Tailwind CSS v4 design system (Next.js first) with free components and paid Pro components/templates. This server installs component source directly into the user's project — no terminal needed.

Typical flow:
1. In a project without BoardUI, call init_boardui once (installs Tailwind v4 + runtime deps, writes styles/ and utils/).
2. Discover with list_components; read source/props with get_component; get working code with get_usage_examples.
3. Install with install_components — it writes the files and installs npm deps.

Component names are exact — when unsure, call list_components instead of guessing.

## RTL Support

BoardUI supports Arabic, Hebrew, and other right-to-left languages across free components, Pro blocks, and templates. The same source handles RTL and LTR; there is no RTL CLI flag or separate component version.

1. Read get_component and get_usage_examples for the free `direction` item. Install it with install_components (stdio), or write its source and dependencies yourself (read-only HTTP). CLI equivalent: `npx boardui@latest add direction`.
2. Wrap the app with DirectionProvider using an explicit BCP 47 locale: `ar` for Arabic, `he` for Hebrew, `en-US` for English. Set matching `lang` and `dir` on `<html>` for a full-app RTL layout. CSS dir alone does not configure React Aria keyboard navigation, calendars, or portalled menus.

```tsx
import { DirectionProvider } from "@/components/foundations/direction/direction";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="ar" dir="rtl">
      <body>
        <DirectionProvider locale="ar">{children}</DirectionProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

3. Use logical styles such as ps/pe, ms/me, start/end, and text-start/text-end. Mirror navigation arrows and drawer motion; preserve physical coordinates for charts, canvas, and decorative art. Custom portals should carry `dir={useDirection()}` on their root. Nest DirectionProvider for mixed-language regions.
4. Keep email addresses, URLs, OTP digits, and code LTR; isolate mixed text with bdi or dir=auto. Choose fonts with Arabic or Hebrew coverage and avoid extra letter spacing for Arabic. Translate application labels and accessible names in the application's translation layer; use Intl for dates, numbers, and currencies. Optional `template-copy` supplies TemplateCopyProvider for translating template display copy. Chinese (`zh-CN`) remains LTR.
5. For older installations, refresh the provider, component source, shared dependencies, and global styles. Preserve customizations before using overwrite. Pro updates use the licensed CLI or updated source downloads.

Setup and live Arabic/Hebrew examples: https://www.boardui.com/rtl

Design rules (always apply when writing UI in a BoardUI project): style with BoardUI's semantic Tailwind tokens, never raw palette classes or hex — text via text-text-primary/-secondary/-tertiary, surfaces via bg-background-*-default/-hover, borders via border-border-* and border-separator-border, icons via text-foreground-icon-*. Type uses composite utilities (text-title-2-medium, text-headline-medium, text-body-medium, ...) that set size/weight/line-height together — never rebuild them from text-sm font-medium. Dark mode flips tokens automatically via the .dark class; never hardcode dark: colors. Merge classes with cx() from @/utils/cx (or the utils alias configured in boardui.json); icons from @remixicon/react as component references. init_boardui installs these rules as always-on files (AGENTS.md + .cursor/rules/boardui.mdc) so they survive beyond this session; install_rules adds them to an already initialized project.

Monorepos/custom aliases: put boardui.json next to the destination package's package.json, and pass that package as projectDir. Installs read its paths/aliases and keep npm dependencies in that package. Pass projectDir to get_component and get_usage_examples too for matching source and examples. Package exports and each consuming app's stylesheet/Tailwind setup must already be wired by th… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Ghostfeed
Ghostfeed agent API. Workflow guidance is available through list_skills/get_skill, native skill resources and matching MCP prompts; load the relevant skill when composing a workflow. Call get_me and list_workspaces first. Reads use the connection default when workspace is omitted; every workspace-scoped write must explicitly pass workspace. Resolve workspace names through list_workspaces and Brand names through list_brands; these identities are distinct and must not be treated as interchangeable. When available in the host, use the matching render_* app tool to show the avatar builder, inspirations, generations, crop editor, or image/video results. Without App tools, use returned media and dashboard URLs. Do not build a replacement Ghostfeed UI or call the Ghostfeed HTTP API from generated presentation code.

## claude.ai Higgsfield
Recipe/setup slashes: get_preset_instructions before other workflows; unambiguous model slashes: models_explore; unknowns: resolve. For 3D scenes or location angles, first call get_preset_instructions with { preset: "/3d-jutsu" }. After verifying a completed Katana video, call show_result with action "katana_video" and media_id or url. Generic Marketing Studio, UGC/ads/posters/marketplace: show_marketing_studio_v2. Browsing never authorizes execute_preset. Creation: generate_image, generate_video, generate_audio. Attached media without media_id: if readable in your sandbox, upload it yourself: media_upload, curl PUT, media_confirm (overrides widget steps); else call media_upload_widget as the only tool in that turn. Resume after upload. Mixed image/video: type:'auto', multiple:true. Voice: create_voice. Higgsfield Genjutsu routes through generate_video: motion transfer -> hf_mult_motion_control; object replacement -> hf_mult_replace_object. For top/popular/trending Genjutsu, first get_presets source=genjutsu category=genjutsu-trending; never legacy motion_control or ad-multiplier for one Genjutsu edit. Without an explicit preset recipe, for multi-step videos call get_workflow_instructions first (with no argument). For clip edits call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "ad-multiplier" } first. AI Influencer: ai_influencer_prepare then ai_influencer_generate. Character sheets: call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "character-sheet" }; websites/apps/games: call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "website-builder-flow" }. Character sheets require explicit requests. Bundled files: get_workflow_bundle_file. For AI Influencer chat creation, use ai_influencer_get_options for explicit traits, ai_influencer_list_presets for examples, or ai_influencer_get_settings with job_id for an existing sheet. ai_influencer_prepare returns design and price without generation. Preserve references and seed; use randomize=false for exact settings. Pass prepared params unchanged to ai_influencer_generate with max_credits at the quote or a lower user budget. Existing creation intent permits proceeding within budget; preview-only requests must stop after preparation. For explicit free-only intent, require known available free_gens_remaining and use_free_gens=true with max_credits=0; never fall back to credits. For variants, prepare each sheet and respect total count and aggregate budget. The generator opens an auto-updating widget for progress and the completed sheet. Wait with jobs_wait (timeout_seconds <= 15); do not duplicate the display with show_generation_by_ids or job_display unless explicitly requested. Offer Genjutsu animation afterward unless declined; require agreement and selection of the exact completed character before get_presets source=genjutsu category=genjutsu with initial_inputs.character_sheet=[{id:job_id,type:image_job}]. Opening that gallery does not authorize video submission. If chat creation is unavailable, report it without silently switching to generic image generation or the builder UI. Multiple independent generations: batch tools, jobs_wait, then one show_generation_by_ids. Use generate_3d to turn an image into a 3D GLB mesh. When unsure which model fits, call models_explore(action:'recommend') before calling a generate_* tool. Use virality_predictor when the user asks to predict video virality or analyze engagement, attention, audience response, retention risk, hook strength, or creative performance. For other existing-asset edits use upscale_image/video, outpaint_image, reframe, remove_background, relight_image, or motion_control (single-character Kling recast). For voice creation in Apps UI-capable clients, call create_voice … [truncated]

## slide-studio
First call list_editors and use the registered local browser tab. Never open or connect CarouselBot through a sandboxed agent browser. If no editor is listed, retry briefly because browser reconnection is automatic, then ask the user to open https://carousel.bot in their normal browser and click Connect AI. Companion compatibility and reconnects are automatic. Do not parallel-retry an action that reports an unsupported internal action; retry once after list_editors so automatic recovery can finish. Never restart a healthy companion for a transient editor disconnect. Before edits call get_design_guidance, then begin_edit_session; pass editSessionId to every edit and end it in cleanup. Parallel workers can share the same browser tab and project; sessions track targets without exclusive locks. Use render_slide to inspect actual pixels.

Each call shells out to `claude -p --model <exact id> --output-format json --tools "" --system-prompt ... --setting-sources "" --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence` in an empty temp cwd. """Token baseline: per-case median tokens measured at the good commit, and the budget rule built on it.

File format (a superset of the target harness's `baseline.json`, so the same file is also passed to the harness via
`--baseline`): {schema_version, commit, good_sha, agent_model, judge_model, repeats, created_at, date, token_factor,
max_steps, cases: {id: {median_tokens, median_steps, n}}}.

BUDGET RULE (used by the runner, the bisect and the revert test):
  * a budget signature (`budget:tokens...` / `budget:steps...`) runs every one of its cases `budget_repeats` times
    (AGENTBISECT_BUDGET_REPEATS, default 3) per commit; behavioural signatures stay at `repeats` (default 1);
  * per case, the commit's metric is the MEDIAN over those repeats; the case is over budget when that median
    exceeds the limit (tokens: `token_factor` x the case's baseline median; steps: `max_steps`);
  * a commit's pass rate for the signature is the fraction of its cases within budget (a case is weighted by its
    executed runs, i.e. equally unless a repeat errored), and the usual confidence band (good >= 0.85, bad <= 0.5) turns it into good / bad / flaky.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import statistics
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

DEFAULT_TOKEN_FACTOR = 1.5


class BaselineError(RuntimeError):
    """The token baseline is missing, unreadable, or does not belong to this investigation."""


def budget_kind(key: str | None) -> str | None:
    """`budget:tokens@order_status` -> 'tokens'; None for any non-budget signature key."""
    m = re.match(r"budget:(\w+)", key or "")
    return m.group(1) if m else None


class Baseline:
    def __init__(self, data: dict[str, Any], path: str | None = None):
        self.data, self.path = data, path
        self.cases: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = data.get("cases") or {}
        self.token_factor = float(data.get("token_factor") or DEFAULT_TOKEN_FACTOR)
        self.max_steps = int(data["max_steps"]) if data.get("max_steps") else None  # else the runs' own cap

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> "Baseline":
        p = Path(path)
        try:
            return cls(json.loads(p.read_text()), str(p))
        except OSError as e:
            raise BaselineError(f"cannot read baseline {p}: {e}") from e
        except ValueError as e:
            raise BaselineError(f"baseline {p} is not valid JSON: {e}") from e

    def validate(self, good_sha: str | None, agent_model: str | None) -> "Baseline":
        """Refuse a baseline that was not measured at THIS investigation's good commit with the pinned agent model:
        a token budget against another commit's or model's medians would be meaningless."""
        where = self.path or "baseline"
        have = self.data.get("good_sha")
        if not have:
            raise BaselineError(f"{where} has no good_sha: it was not written by `agentbisect calibrate`")
        if not good_sha or not _same_sha(have, good_sha):
            raise BaselineError(f"{where} was calibrated at {have[:10]} but this investigation's good commit is "
                                f"{(good_sha or '?')[:10]}: run `agentbisect calibrate` at the good commit")
        if not self.data.get("agent_model") or self.data["agent_model"] != agent_model:
            raise BaselineError(f"{where} was calibrated with agent model {self.data.get('agent_model')!r} but the "
                                f"pinned agent model is {agent_model!r}")
        if not self.cases:
            raise BaselineError(f"{where} has no per-case medians")
        return self

    def median_tokens(self, case: str) -> float | None:
        c = self.cases.get(case)
        return float(c["median_tokens"]) if c and c.get("median_tokens") is not None else None

    def limit(self, kind: str, case: str) -> float | None:
        if kind == "tokens":
            m = self.median_tokens(case)
            return None if m is None else self.token_factor * m
        if kind == "steps":
            return None if self.max_steps is None else float(self.max_steps)
        return None


def _same_sha(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    return min(len(a), len(b)) >= 7 and (a.startswith(b) or b.startswith(a))


def need_baseline_message(sig_key: str) -> str:
    return (f"budget signature {sig_key} needs a token baseline from the good commit: run `agentbisect calibrate "
            "--repo R --good SHA` once and point AGENTBISECT_BASELINE at the file it writes (never recalibrated "
            "automatically)")


def build_baseline(entries: dict[str, dict], good_sha: str, models: dict[str, str], repeats: int,
                   skipped: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """entries: case -> verdict-cache aggregate at the good commit. Medians use only the runs whose deterministic
    checks passed (a budget miss does not disqualify a run), like the target harness's own calibration."""
    cases: dict[str, dict] = {}
    caps: list[int] = []
    excluded = dict(skipped or {})
    for case, e in sorted(entries.items()):
        ok = [d for d in e.get("detail") or [] if d.get("status") in ("pass", "fail") and d.get("tokens") is not None
              and all(f.startswith("budget:") for f in d.get("fails") or [])]
        if not ok:
            excluded[case] = "no run passed its deterministic checks (or reported tokens)"
            continue
        steps = [d["steps"] for d in ok if d.get("steps") is not None]
        caps += [d["max_steps"] for d in ok if d.get("max_steps")]
        cases[case] = {"median_tokens": statistics.median(d["tokens"] for d in ok),
                       "median_steps": statistics.median(steps) if steps else None, "n": len(ok)}
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return {"schema_version": 1, "commit": good_sha, "good_sha": good_sha, "agent_model": models.get("agent_model"),
            "judge_model": models.get("judge_model"), "repeats": repeats, "provider": "anthropic",
            "created_at": now.isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "date": now.date().isoformat(),
            "token_factor": DEFAULT_TOKEN_FACTOR, "max_steps": max(caps) if caps else None, "cases": cases,
            "excluded_cases": excluded}


def calibrate(runner: Any, good_sha: str, cases: list[str], out: str | Path, run_id: str = "calibrate") -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run the good commit once (`budget_repeats` per case, no baseline passed to the harness), write the per-case
    median tokens to `out` and return the baseline dict. Never called implicitly."""
    cfg = runner.cfg
    saved = cfg.baseline, runner.signature
    cfg.baseline, runner.signature = None, None  # no baseline for the harness while measuring one
    try:  # budget_cases: every case at exactly budget_repeats, never escalated
        res = runner.evaluate_commit(good_sha, run_id, cases, budget_cases=cases)
    finally:
        cfg.baseline, runner.signature = saved
    if res.verdict == "skip" and not res.executed:
        raise BaselineError(f"cannot calibrate at {good_sha[:10]}: {res.reason}")
    entries, skipped = {}, {}
    for c in cases:
        e = runner.cache.get(good_sha, c, cfg.models) or {}
        if "skip" in e:
            skipped[c] = f"skipped by the target: {e['skip']}"
        elif e:
            entries[c] = e
        else:
            skipped[c] = "no executed runs (every repeat errored)"
    data = build_baseline(entries, good_sha, cfg.models, cfg.budget_repeats, skipped)
    if res.verdict != "good":
        data["warnings"] = [f"the good commit evaluated as {res.verdict} (pass rate {res.pass_rate}): is it really good?"]
    if not data["cases"]:
        raise BaselineError("no case produced a usable token measurement; nothing written")
    Path(out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    Path(out).write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n")
    return data


def median_over_budget(values: list[float], limit: float | None) -> bool | None:
    """The budget rule for one case: median of the repeats vs the limit; None when it cannot be decided."""
    if not values or limit is None:
        return None
    return statistics.median(values) > limit
"""One row per failure signature: culprit, revert test before/after, smart vs plain rounds. Built only from saved
state (nothing is hardcoded or compared against expected answers), so the table of a final re-run reads the same
way as any other run. Used by `agentbisect summary` and by the per-signature section of the reports."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from typing import Any

from .bisect import KNOWN_PREEXISTING
from .models import BisectState
from .state import StateError, StateStore

HEAD = ["signature", "outcome", "revert test (before -> after)", "smart vs plain (eval rounds)"]


def _num(v: Any) -> str:
    return "n/a" if v is None else f"{v:,.0f}" if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and abs(v) >= 100 else f"{v:g}"


def _pct(v: Any) -> str:
    return "n/a" if v is None else f"{v * 100:.0f}%"


def revert_cell(st: BisectState) -> str:
    c, rt = st.culprit, st.metrics.get("revert_test") or {}
    if not c or "revert_test" not in st.metrics:
        return "not run"
    verdict = {True: "PASSED", False: "FAILED", None: "inconclusive"}[c.revert_test_passed]
    b = rt.get("budget")
    if b:
        bef, aft = b.get("before") or {}, b.get("after") or {}
        kind = aft.get("kind") or bef.get("kind") or "metric"
        return (f"{verdict}: median {kind} {_num(bef.get('median'))} -> {_num(aft.get('median'))}, "
                f"within budget {bef.get('within')}/{bef.get('total')} -> {aft.get('within')}/{aft.get('total')}")
    if rt.get("reverted_pass_rate") is None:
        return verdict
    return f"{verdict}: pass {_pct(rt.get('culprit_pass_rate'))} -> {_pct(rt['reverted_pass_rate'])}"


def rounds_cell(st: BisectState) -> str:
    cmp_ = st.metrics.get("comparison")
    if not cmp_ or "plain" not in cmp_ or "smart" not in cmp_:
        return "n/a (no compare data)"
    p, s = cmp_["plain"], cmp_["smart"]
    same = "" if cmp_.get("same_culprit") in (None, True) else ", DIFFERENT culprit"
    return f"{p.get('eval_rounds')} plain vs {s.get('eval_rounds')} smart{same}"


def outcome_cell(st: BisectState) -> str:
    if st.status == "refused" or st.metrics.get("known_preexisting"):
        return KNOWN_PREEXISTING
    if st.culprit:
        return f"culprit {st.culprit.sha[:10]} (confidence {st.culprit.confidence or '?'})"
    if st.status == "failed":
        return f"failed: {(st.error or 'unknown error')[:120]}"
    return st.status


def summary_rows(states: list[BisectState]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    out = []
    for st in states:  # caller's order: store.list() is by creation, group_states() is primary first
        sig = st.spec.signature if st.spec else None
        out.append({"id": st.id, "signature": sig.key if sig else "(whole-case pass rate)", "status": st.status,
                    "outcome": outcome_cell(st), "culprit": st.culprit.sha if st.culprit else None,
                    "revert": revert_cell(st), "rounds": rounds_cell(st)})
    return out


def cells(r: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    return [r["signature"], r["outcome"], r["revert"], r["rounds"]]


def render_text(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    if not rows:
        return "no investigations"
    table = [HEAD, *map(cells, rows)]
    w = [max(len(row[i]) for row in table) for i in range(len(HEAD))]
    fmt = lambda row: "  ".join(c.ljust(w[i]) for i, c in enumerate(row)).rstrip()  # noqa: E731
    return "\n".join([fmt(table[0]), fmt(["-" * x for x in w]), *map(fmt, table[1:])])


def render_markdown(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    esc = lambda s: str(s).replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ")  # noqa: E731
    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(HEAD) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(HEAD)]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(esc(c) for c in cells(r)) + " |" for r in rows]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def render(rows: list[dict[str, Any]], fmt: str = "text") -> str:
    return {"text": render_text, "md": render_markdown, "json": lambda r: json.dumps(r, indent=2)}[fmt](rows)


def group_states(store: StateStore, st: BisectState) -> list[BisectState]:
    """The investigation plus its sibling signatures (primary and siblings of one `investigate` call)."""
    try:
        root = store.load(st.metrics["signature_group"]) if st.metrics.get("signature_group") else st
    except StateError:
        root = st
    ids = [root.id, *[x["id"] for x in root.metrics.get("signature_siblings", [])]]
    out = []
    for i in dict.fromkeys(ids):
        try:
            out.append(st if i == st.id else store.load(i))
        except StateError:
            pass
    return out or [st]

142	def _tools_in(v: Any, depth: int = 0) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
143	    """Tool calls found in a payload: OpenAI `tool_calls`, Anthropic `tool_use` blocks, plain {tool|tool_name}."""
144	    out: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []
145	    if depth > 6 or v is None:
146	        return out
147	    if isinstance(v, list):
148	        for x in v:
149	            out += _tools_in(x, depth + 1)
150	    elif isinstance(v, dict):
151	        if v.get("type") == "tool_use" and v.get("name"):
152	            out.append((str(v["name"]), v.get("input") if isinstance(v.get("input"), dict) else {}))
153	        elif isinstance(v.get("function"), dict) and v["function"].get("name"):
154	            a = v["function"].get("arguments")
155	            if isinstance(a, str):
156	                try:
157	                    a = json.loads(a)
158	                except ValueError:
159	                    a = {}
160	            out.append((str(v["function"]["name"]), a if isinstance(a, dict) else {}))
161	        elif v.get("tool_name") or (v.get("tool") and isinstance(v["tool"], str)):
162	            out.append((str(v.get("tool_name") or v["tool"]), v.get("args") if isinstance(v.get("args"), dict) else {}))
163	        else:
164	            for x in v.values():
165	                out += _tools_in(x, depth + 1)
166	    return out

170	    """Tolerant normaliser (fixture dicts and neatlogs span items; payload fields `input`/`output` optional)."""

172	    kind = str(d.get("kind") or d.get("spanKind") or attrs.get("openinference.span.kind") or "").lower()
173	    raw = d.get("tools") or d.get("tool_calls") or []
174	    if raw and all(isinstance(t, str) for t in raw):  # recorded spans: plain tool names
175	        found = [(t, d.get("args") or {}) for t in raw]
176	    else:

180	    if not found:

182	    return Span(name=str(d.get("name") or d.get("spanName") or ""), kind="tool" if found and not kind else kind,
183	                tools=[n for n, _ in found], args=dict(found[0][1]) if found else {},
184	                text=(_text_of(d.get("output")) or _text_of(d.get("input")) or "")[:500])

224	class NeatlogsCliSource(TraceSource):
225	    """Reads through the neatlogs public-API CLI (`traces list|get|payload`, `detections get|hits|trends`).
226	
227	    The project key used by the SDK does not authenticate CLI reads; the user must have run
228	    `neatlogs --host ... --profile neatlogs-us --credential-source profile auth login --device`."""
229	
230	    def __init__(self, project: str | None = None, binary: str = NEATLOGS_BIN, host: str = NEATLOGS_HOST,
231	                 profile: str = NEATLOGS_PROFILE, run: Run | None = None,
232	                 sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep):
233	        self._sleep = sleep
234	        self.project = project or os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID")
235	        self.binary, self.host, self.profile = binary, host, profile
236	        self._run = run or _subprocess_run
237	
238	    def _call(self, *args: str, retry: bool = True) -> Any:
239	        """One CLI call; a freshly ingested trace answers TRACE_PROCESSING ("still being finalized"), so retry it."""
240	        for attempt in range(PROCESSING_RETRIES + 1 if retry else 1):
241	            try:
242	                return self._call_once(*args)
243	            except IntakeError as e:
244	                if "TRACE_PROCESSING" not in str(e) or attempt >= PROCESSING_RETRIES or not retry:
245	                    raise
246	                self._sleep(PROCESSING_WAIT_S * (attempt + 1))
247	
248	    def _call_once(self, *args: str) -> Any:
249	        argv = [self.binary, "--host", self.host, "--profile", self.profile, "--credential-source", "profile",
250	                "--json"]
251	        if self.project:
252	            argv += ["--project", self.project]
253	        try:
254	            rc, out, err = self._run(argv + list(args))
255	        except FileNotFoundError as e:
256	            raise IntakeError(f"neatlogs CLI not found at {self.binary}") from e
257	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
258	            raise IntakeError(f"neatlogs CLI timed out: {' '.join(args)}") from e
259	        body: Any = None
260	        for blob in (out, err):
261	            try:
262	                body = json.loads(blob)
263	                break
264	            except (ValueError, TypeError):
265	                continue
266	        code = body.get("code") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
267	        if rc != 0 or code:
268	            text = f"{out}\n{err}"
269	            if code in _AUTH_CODES or (code is None and _AUTH_TEXT.search(text)):
270	                raise WaitingOnHumanLogin(
271	                    "waiting on human login: neatlogs CLI is not authenticated. Run "
272	                    f"`{self.binary} --host {self.host} --profile {self.profile} --credential-source profile "
273	                    "auth login --device` and approve the device code in the browser, then retry.")
274	            if code == "MISSING_PROJECT_ID":
275	                raise IntakeError("neatlogs project id missing: pass --project <uuid> or set NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID")
276	            raise IntakeError(f"neatlogs CLI failed ({code or rc}): {(err or out).strip()[:300]}")
277	        return _unwrap(body)

279	    def _paged(self, key: str, *args: str, limit: int) -> list[dict]:
280	        data = self._call(*args, "--limit", str(min(limit, 50)), "--all", "--max-items", str(limit))
281	        return list(data.get(key, [])) if isinstance(data, dict) else list(data or [])

283	    def get_trace(self, trace_id: str) -> Trace:
284	        t = trace_from_dict(self._call("traces", "get", trace_id))
285	        if t.input is None:
286	            try:
287	                t.input = self._root_input(trace_id)
288	            except IntakeError:  # e.g. TRACE_PROCESSING: spans not readable yet; the case tag still identifies the case
289	                pass
290	        return t

292	    def _root_input(self, trace_id: str) -> str | None:
293	        spans = self._call("traces", "spans", "list", trace_id, "--limit", "50", retry=False)
294	        roots = [s for s in spans.get("spans", []) if not s.get("parentSpanId")] if isinstance(spans, dict) else []
295	        for s in roots[:1]:
296	            p = self._call("traces", "payload", trace_id, s["spanId"], "--fields", "input")
297	            v = ((p.get("fields") or {}).get("input") or {}) if isinstance(p, dict) else {}
298	            if v.get("available"):
299	                return _text_of(v.get("value"))
300	        return None

302	    def spans(self, trace_id: str) -> list[Span]:
303	        """Spans in start order; LLM/tool payloads are fetched to find chosen tools (shape UNVERIFIED on real runs)."""
304	        data = self._call("traces", "spans", "list", trace_id, "--limit", "50")
305	        items = data.get("spans", []) if isinstance(data, dict) else []
306	        items = sorted(items, key=lambda s: str(s.get("startTime") or s.get("startedAt") or ""))
307	        out = []
308	        for s in items:
309	            if not s.get("parentSpanId"):
310	                continue  # the root run span only wraps the steps
311	            d = dict(s)
312	            try:
313	                p = self._call("traces", "payload", trace_id, s["spanId"], "--fields", "output")
314	                v = ((p.get("fields") or {}).get("output") or {}) if isinstance(p, dict) else {}
315	                d["output"] = v.get("value") if v.get("available") else None
316	            except IntakeError:
317	                pass
318	            out.append(span_from_dict(d))
319	        return out

322	        args = ["traces", "list"] + (["--workflow", workflow] if workflow else [])
323	        return [trace_from_dict(d) for d in self._paged("traces", *args, limit=limit)]

344	    Pass a dict or a path to a .json file."""
345	
346	    def __init__(self, data: dict[str, Any] | str | Path):
347	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
348	            data = json.loads(Path(data).read_text())

352	        self.fail_auth = bool(data.get("auth_failure"))

359	        self._check()

362	        return self.traces[trace_id]

371	        return sorted(ts, key=lambda t: t.started_at, reverse=True)[:limit]

382	
383	    def detection_trend(self, detection_id: str, start: str, end: str, granularity: str = "day") -> list[dict]:

for tool, want_s, saw_s in _CALL_ARGS.findall(reason):
        try:
            want, saw = ast.literal_eval(want_s), ast.literal_eval(saw_s)
        except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
            out.append({"key": f"call_args:{tool}", "detail": tool, "expected": "", "got": ""})
            continue
        if not saw:
            out.append({"key": f"call_args:{tool}", "detail": tool, "expected": "a call", "got": "no call"})
            continue
        bad = [k for k, v in want.items() if not any(_same(c.get(k), v) for c in saw)]
        for k in bad or list(want):
            out.append({"key": f"call_args:{tool}.{k}", "detail": f"{tool}.{k}", "expected": str(want[k]),
                        "got": str(saw[0].get(k))})
    return out


def failure_records(check: str, reason: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    base = {"check": check, "reason": reason[:300]}
    if check == "call_args":
        recs = _call_args_failures(reason)
        if recs:
            return [{**base, **r} for r in recs]
    return [{**base, "key": check, "detail": "", "expected": "", "got": ""}]


def failures_of_result(r: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Failure records for one harness result dict (empty for passing runs). A failing run with no recorded
    cause still gets a generic `case_fail` record so it is never silently treated as a pass."""
    out: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for c in r.get("checks") or []:
        if not c.get("passed", True):
            out += failure_records(str(c.get("check")), str(c.get("reason") or ""))
    b = r.get("budget") or {}
    if b.get("status") == "fail":
        reason = str(b.get("reason") or "")
        kinds = [k for k in ("steps", "tokens") if k in reason] or ["steps"]
        cat = f"@{r['category']}" if r.get("category") else ""
        out += [{"key": f"budget:{k}{cat}", "check": "budget", "detail": f"{k}{cat}", "expected": "", "got": "",
                 "reason": reason[:300]} for k in kinds]
    j = r.get("judge")
    if isinstance(j, dict) and j.get("passed") is False:
        out.append({"key": "judge", "check": "judge", "detail": "", "expected": "", "got": "",
                    "reason": str(j.get("reason") or "")[:300]})
    if not out and r.get("status") == "fail":
        out.append({"key": "case_fail", "check": "case_fail", "detail": "", "expected": "", "got": "",
                    "reason": str(r.get("reason") or "")[:300]})
    return out


def signature_from_record(rec: dict[str, str]) -> FailureSignature:
    return FailureSignature(key=rec["key"], check=rec.get("check", ""), detail=rec.get("detail", ""),
                            expected=rec.get("expected", ""), got=rec.get("got", ""), reason=rec.get("reason", ""))


def signature_from_key(key: str) -> FailureSignature:
    """For `--signature KEY` on the command line."""
    check, _, detail = key.partition(":")
    return FailureSignature(key=key, check=check, detail=detail)


def signatures_of(result: CommitResult) -> list[FailureSignature]:
    """All failing checks seen at a commit, one signature each, most frequent first."""
    sigs = [FailureSignature.from_dict(d) for d in result.failure_signatures]
    return sorted(sigs, key=lambda s: (-s.fails, s.key))


def group_signatures(infos: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], case_runs: dict[str, int],
                     case_fails: dict[str, dict[str, int]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """infos: key -> first-seen record; case_fails: case -> {key: failing runs}; case_runs: case -> executed runs.
    -> signature dicts with the cases where the key fires and run counts over those cases."""
    by_key: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for case, ks in case_fails.items():
        for k, n in ks.items():
            if n > 0:
                by_key[k].append(case)
    out = []
    for k, cases in by_key.items():
        cases = sorted(cases)
        s = signature_from_record(infos.get(k) or {"key": k})
        s.cases = cases
        s.fails = sum(case_fails[c][k] for c in cases)
        s.runs = sum(case_runs.get(c, 0) for c in cases)
        out.append(s.to_dict())
    return out


def pick_primary(sigs: Iterable[FailureSignature], bad_case: str | None) -> FailureSignature | None:
    """The signature to bisect first: one that fires in the bad trace's case, else any. A wrong behaviour (a
    deterministic check) outranks a cost miss (budget), since the report of a bad trace is about wrong output;
    then the most frequent. The others are bisected as siblings."""
    sigs = sorted(sigs, key=lambda s: (s.check == "budget", s.check == "judge", -s.fails, s.key))
    if bad_case:
        mine = [s for s in sigs if bad_case in s.cases]
        if mine:
            return mine[0]
    return sigs[0] if sigs else None


def signature_from_trace(metadata: dict[str, Any], tags: list[str]) -> FailureSignature | None:
    """A trace that carries its own failing check: metadata `failed_checks` ([{check, reason}]) or a
    `check:<key>` tag. Real neatlogs traces do not carry this today; the bad end's eval result is used then."""
    for fc in metadata.get("failed_checks") or []:
        if isinstance(fc, dict) and fc.get("check"):
            return signature_from_record(failure_records(str(fc["check"]), str(fc.get("reason") or ""))[0])
    for t in tags:
        if t.startswith("check:") and len(t) > 6:
            return signature_from_key(t[6:])
    return None


# -- planner feed --

def symptom_text(sig: FailureSignature) -> str:
    """Words for the planner's intent scoring."""
    if sig.check == "case_fail":  # no specific check known: nothing to add to the symptom
        return ""
    bits = [sig.check, sig.detail.replace(".", " ").replace("_", " "), sig.reason]
    if sig.expected or sig.got:
        bits += [f"expected {sig.expected}", f"got {sig.got}"]
    e, g = _try_float(sig.expected), _try_float(sig.got)
    if e and g and (abs(g / e - 100) < 1e-6 or abs(g / e - 0.01) < 1e-9):  # 64.0 vs 6400: a units mix-up
        bits.append("cents dollars unit conversion")
    return " ".join(b for b in bits if b)


def _try_float(v: str) -> float | None:
    try:
        return float(v)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def symbol_hints(sig: FailureSignature) -> list[str]:
    """Names to look up with `entire graph impact`: the tool behind a call_args failure, plus refund/amount
    vocabulary when the failing value is a money amount."""
    hints: list[str] = []
    if sig.check == "call_args" and sig.detail:
        tool = sig.detail.split(".")[0]
        hints += [tool, f"_tool_{tool}"]
    text = f"{sig.detail} {sig.reason}".lower()
    hints += [w for w in ("refund", "amount") if w in text]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(hints))


# -- overlapping regressions: one investigation per signature --

def spawn_siblings(store: StateStore, st: BisectState) -> list[BisectState]:
    """After the primary investigation discovered several failing checks at the bad end, create one more
    investigation per remaining signature (same repo, range, strategy; shared verdict cache, so commits already
    evaluated for the cases they share cost nothing). Idempotent: siblings are recorded on the primary."""
    from .models import RegressionSpec
    found = [FailureSignature.from_dict(d) for d in st.metrics.get("signatures", [])]
    mine = st.spec.signature.key if st.spec and st.spec.signature else None
    done = {x["key"]: x["id"] for x in st.metrics.get("signature_siblings", [])}
    made = []
    for sig in found:
        if sig.key == mine or sig.key in done:
            continue
        spec = RegressionSpec.from_dict({**st.spec.to_dict(), "signature": sig.to_dict()})
        sib = store.create(st.repo, spec=spec, good_sha=st.good_sha, bad_sha=st.bad_sha)
        sib.metrics.update(strategy=st.metrics.get("strategy", "plain"), source=st.metrics.get("source"),
                           signature_group=st.id, signatures_discovered=True)
        store.save(sib)
        st.metrics.setdefault("signature_siblings", []).append({"id": sib.id, "key": sig.key})
        made.append(sib)
    store.save(st)
    return made
